thread.title: JUDGE'S CLASSIC HOME RUN LEADS TO NOTHING: THE YANKEES SHOULD FIRE AARON BOONE
thread.title_full: JUDGE'S CLASSIC HOME RUN LEADS TO NOTHING: THE YANKEES SHOULD FIRE AARON BOONE

author: Jay Mariotti
title: JUDGE'S CLASSIC HOME RUN LEADS TO NOTHING: THE YANKEES SHOULD FIRE AARON BOONE
text:
Consider it the greatest home run that led to absolutely nothing. Aaron Judge rocked the left-field foul pole with a mammoth shot that made him suggest historically Tuesday night, “I guess a couple of ghosts out there in Monument Park helped kind of keep that fair.” Well, if there were spirits inside Yankee Stadium, they didn’t show up Wednesday night.
The home team fell for the 16th straight postseason, which is much too long when the Yankees have won 27 World Series, losing to a Toronto team that used a bullpenning crew of Varland, Fluharty, Dominguez, Lauer, Rodriguez, Little, Fisher and Hoffman. They scored twice and let the Blue Jays advance to the American League Championship Series, against Seattle or Detroit, in a nation that is burying Canada with tariff wars. To think they bounced the Yankees — a team President Trump has supported for decades — probably doesn’t bode well if they intend to win a title and host a parade. Timothee Chalamet did not show up with a shaved head, alongside Kylie Jenner, to see a 5-2 loss.
So at this point, owner Hal Steinbrenner must make a decision that his father, George, would have grasped years ago. Aaron Boone cannot continue as the manager when Judge, after a career of postseason mishaps, finally produced thunder and could not inspire his teammates. This team is too tight and wobbly, which led Giancarlo Stanton to scream in an August meltdown, and we’ve seen Boone blow up so many times at umpires that we simply start laughing. He is not the quintessential Manager of the Yankees, which we’ve seen in older movies. And if that person actually exists, this franchise is too glorified in sports Americana to not find him.
“The ending is the worst, especially when you know you have a really good group. It was a team that played for one another and got beat here. Credit to the Blue Jays,” Boone said. “It’s a beat-up room in there. This has been a tough year for me personally, and for all that you go through, for it to end abruptly is always difficult. It’s a beautiful game that means so much to so many inside our organization, to have a chance to win a championship. When it ends this way, it’s terrible. But I know for me personally, it continues to ignite your fire and have a chance at that glory.”
But then he said, “You don’t win games on emotion all the time.”
This was a game that should have centered on emotion.
In Los Angeles, the Dodgers hold a 2-1 lead over the Phillies after an 8-2 loss and still should proceed to another Series. The Yankees lost to Vladimir Guerrero Jr. and a team that hasn’t played for a championship since winning back to back crowns in 1992 and 1993. He signed a $500 million contract this year, making him the third-highest-paid player in the sport. We’d better pay attention. “My goal always is to win a World Series,” Guerrero said. “To bring the World Series here.”
To Canada, which only roils New York. Fans at Rogers Centre ignore the “Star-Spangled Banner” until the singer reaches the final notes, when they cheer. They are angry at Trump and view this victory as thrashing him. “The atmosphere here is — you kind of have to be here to understand it,” manager John Schneider said. “It’s something this group does not take lightly. It’s something that we as an organization do not take lightly, that we’re playing for a country.”
No one leaving a world-famous ballpark wanted to hear it in the Bronx. All people heard after the Game 3 victory were loud rally cries. “I was just saying, ‘Hit the foul pole,’ ’’ Cody Bellinger said.
“We all went over the video about 10 times in the dugout after he hit it,” Jazz Chisholm Jr. said. “It was crazy. It just shows he’s so unbelievable.”
“It was a best-player-in-the-game type performance,” Boone said.
Said Louis Varland, who allowed the pop: “He made a really good pitch look really bad.”
Guess who started Game 4? Varland. Judge received praise from fans and media and finally said, “I get yelled at for swinging at them out of the zone, but now I’m getting praised for it. It’s a game. You’ve got to go out there and play. I don’t care what the numbers say or where something was at. I’m just up there trying to put a good swing on a good pitch, and it looked good to me.”
But at the finish of the season’s final game, Judge hit a ball off the left-field wall. He was 13 for 25 in the playoffs and had six RBIs against the Jays. His teammates didn’t help. Bellinger struck out swinging and said goodbye for the winter. This team cannot return in the spring with Boone. Otherwise, they aren’t the Yankees any longer.
With Guerrero, George Springer, Shane Bieber, Kevin Gausman and a lot of players you don’t know, the Blue Jays merit your gaze even if you appreciate tariffs. They will have the homefield advantage in the ALCS and should face Tarik Skubal and Detroit. That is, if the Mariners don’t use Game 5 to beat down Skubal, who has lost two games to Seattle this season. He has a 1.84 ERA and 23 strikeouts this postseason. Who wins? Doesn’t America want to see Cal Raleigh hit more homers, including his 61st this year to a man who wore a “Dump 61 Here” t-shirt?
“This is what competition is all about,” Skubal said. “This is why you play the game, for Game 5s. I think that’s going to bring out the best in everyone involved. That’s why this game is so beautiful.”
The Cubs beat Milwaukee, 4-3. So? They’re down 2-1.
“That was a lot of fun to get in there and get four outs and come away with a win,” closer Brad Keller said. “That was such a team effort there. We’re looking forward to doing it again tomorrow.”
The Phillies beat the Dodgers, with Kyle Schwarber homering off the top of the pavilion in right field and hitting another later. So? They’re down 2-1.
“It sounds great, but we still have a job to do tomorrow,” Schwarber said. “We know what’s at stake. We know what we have in our room.”
The major question is how Steinbrenner and general manager Brian Cashman — should he return? — address the Aaron Boone issue. The Yankees lose, the Yankees lose, the Yankees lose.
With no championship ring, at 33, Judge deserves much better.
###
Jay Mariotti, called “without question the most impacting Chicago sportswriter of the past quarter-century,’’ writes general sports columns for Substack while appearing on some of the 1,678,498 podcasts and shows in production today. He is an accomplished columnist, TV panelist and talk/podcast host. Living in Los Angeles, he gravitated by osmosis to film projects.
